rationale: Current Linux/POSIX dependency is limited to the shared secure read-only file-open flags plus audited signal-disposition file-descriptor-limit root-startup privilege-drop startup process-hardening standard UDP socket standard UDP batch and AF_XDP adapter operations.

Current Unix filesystem syscall wrapper is confined to descriptor-relative read-only secret-store root and file traversal with directory and no-follow flags; the first-party boundary remains safe Rust and validates opened handle type and permissions.

OxideGun and BoronDNS server use Aya only behind explicit XDP/AF_XDP feature paths for lab load generation, reply suppression, or server redirect setup; physical NIC production evidence remains a separate release gate.
Future eBPF/XDP support must enter through an audited packet-I/O adapter and a privileged deployment profile.
Future AF_XDP support must enter through an audited packet-I/O adapter and a privileged deployment profile.

OxideGun and BoronDNS server use the pure-Rust xdp crate only behind explicit XDP/AF_XDP feature paths for dedicated Linux test interfaces; physical NIC production evidence remains a separate release gate.
Future io_uring support must enter through an audited packet-I/O adapter with buffer-lifetime and cancellation tests.
Future packed zone-store or mapped-region work must enter through an audited zone-store adapter with bounds and publication tests.
Future zero-copy packed-store or response-cache work must enter through audited adapters with alignment, bounds, TTL, and invalidation tests.

Transitive-only through the current xdp crate; confined to audited OxideGun and BoronDNS AF_XDP adapter boundaries and not available to packed zone-store or response-cache work without a future dependency-gate update.
